nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the main focus of Cultural Theory (CT) as discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Cultural Theory (CT) analyzes how actors perceive the world and interact with their surroundings based on their values and beliefs.
nodes.paragraph: Political cultures point to the importance of mean- ing (Mamadouh, 1999b, p. 477). Cultural Theory (CT) is a long-established approach for such analyses (Thompson et al., 1990). CT, originating from the works of Douglas (1978) and Douglas and Wildavsky (1982) and developed by Thompson et al. (1990), analyzes how actors perceive the world (related risks, problems, solutions, etc.) and interact with their surroundings based on their values and beliefs (Chuang et al., 2020; Tansey, 2004). We set out to explore how CT could assist in understanding the roots of different perceptions in EU forest policy, investigating two main research questions: 1. How do EU forest policy actors envisage forests and their ecosystem services in terms of perceived problems, preferred solutions, and responsibilities to govern forests? Policy Sciences 2. How can Cultural Theory contribute to understanding overlaps and differences in these views and which theoretical implications could a better understanding of these over - laps and differences offer? Theoretical framework: cultural theory Cultural Theory identifies four main politically relevant worldviews: egalitarianism, indi- vidualism, hierarchy, and fatalism.
